title: US Sanctions 50+ Iranian Entities in "Operation Economic Fury" Round 2
detail: The US State Department and Treasury Department sanctioned more than 50 entities — currency exchange houses, front companies, individuals, and 19 vessels — for helping Iran evade international sanctions and fund activities the US designates as destabilizing. The primary target was Amin Exchange, which operated through UAE, Turkey, and China/Hong Kong to launder money for sanctioned Iranian banks. The sanctions were issued under Executive Order 13902, part of the broader Operation Economic Fury campaign launched against Iran's financial infrastructure. The move signaled that sanctions pressure would continue even as diplomatic talks proceeded — a dual-track strategy that Iran's Foreign Ministry criticized as undermining trust in negotiations.

media.caption: US sanctions more than 50 Iranian financial and shipping entities in second round of Operation Economic Fury

title: Araghchi: US "Contradictory and Excessive Stances" Obstruct Peace Talks
detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, meeting with Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in Tehran, publicly stated that Washington's 'contradictory and excessive stances' constitute 'a serious obstacle' to diplomatic progress in the Iran-US negotiations. Araghchi cited deep institutional distrust of the US establishment, rooted in repeated broken promises — including the 2018 JCPOA withdrawal — and said Iran could not accept demands that simultaneously insisted on zero enrichment and continued sanctions pressure. He discussed Iran's revised 14-point proposal submitted through Pakistan and signaled Iran was still committed to negotiations despite the new US sanctions round announced the same day. The remarks illustrated the fundamental tension in Washington's dual-track approach of talks plus economic pressure.

media.caption: Araghchi tells Pakistan's interior minister that US contradictory positions are blocking a peace deal
